explanation: Build a symmetric copy of the supplied edge constraints, then BFS each component using distances from its root. Adjacent BFS levels differ by at most one; an edge within one level makes the parity coloring impossible.
timeComplexity: O(V + E) time. Symmetrizing creates at most two adjacency entries per constraint, then BFS visits each vertex and entry once.
spaceComplexity: O(V + E) auxiliary space. The symmetric graph, coloring state and queue occupy O(V+E).

correctness: In an undirected graph BFS assigns minimum distances, so an edge joins equal or adjacent levels. Equal levels create an odd cycle through the BFS tree; otherwise distance parity gives opposite colors on every edge. Symmetrizing constraints makes this argument hold even when an input edge is listed only once. Every component is searched.
walkthrough: For 0−1−2−3−0 and isolated 4, BFS levels from 0 are 0:{0}, 1:{1,3}, 2:{2}. Every edge joins adjacent levels; vertex 4 forms a separate level-zero component, so return true.
edgeCases: Disconnected and isolated vertices must all be processed.
A self-loop cannot connect opposite groups.
An odd cycle fails; an even cycle does not.
